tagline: Save points for code, for when git is overkill.
summary: A checkpoint tool for projects where full version control is more ceremony than the work deserves — experiments, tutorials and quick prototypes. It snapshots a project's state and restores it, so a risky change can be undone without a branching model.
highlights: Aimed at the cases git is genuinely too heavy for: tutorials, throwaway experiments and rapid prototypes.
Restores a saved checkpoint wholesale, so an experiment is abandoned by restoring rather than by reverting.
Keeps checkpoints outside the project's own history, leaving any existing repository untouched.
